endorsements.quote: It is essential that both healthcare professionals and patients receive a specific disclosure when AI has been used in their diagnosis or treatment process.
RCTs are the highest level of evidence for clinical interventions, and AI solutions for diagnosis/treatment should be assessed to the same standard.

The implication is that all AI healthcare applications should have in‐depth technical documentation including the purpose, procedure of development, comprehensive information on the data sets used for training and validation, similar to the information provided in clinical trials for medication or medical devices.
Measures of effectiveness used for other studies, such as sensitivity, specificity and confidence intervals, should also be used for AI.
Involving patients in the codesign of AI tools can improve their acceptability and usability [ 4 , 26 ].
The perspectives of both patients and clinicians should be sought early and incorporated consistently to maximize utility, trustworthiness, and practical relevance.

unlisted_practices: Establish mechanisms for continuous monitoring and evaluation of AI system performance and efficacy, and improve AI systems based on monitoring and feedback.
Ensure AI assists rather than replaces clinical judgment.
Govern training data to be non-discriminatory so AI does not perpetuate health inequities.
Prioritize AI deployment through a systematic triage strategy focused on high unmet need, disease burden, and data availability.
Ensure AI outputs are explainable to clinicians and patients.
Develop AI applications through cross-disciplinary teams including engineers, ethicists, and patients.
Design patient-facing AI apps with attention to accessibility, health literacy, and data protection.
Adapt AI tools to diverse populations, cultures, and habits.
Conduct prospective studies evaluating clinical utility, real-world performance, and patient-centered outcomes of AI.

screen.reason: This is a consensus/think-tank report (ICI-RS 2025) outlining recommendations, frameworks, and research priorities for implementing and governing AI in the management of lower urinary tract dysfunction.
